title: Early cacao use and domestication at Santa Ana-La Florida
summary: At Santa Ana-La Florida in southeast Ecuador, evidence dating from approximately 5,300 years ago shows cacao use, identified through starch grains, absorbed theobromine residues and ancient DNA. The researchers conclude that the site residents were involved in cacao domestication and name the upper Amazon as the oldest centre of cacao domestication yet identified.

uncertainty.note: Source says "approximately 5,300 years ago"; calibration convention not stated on the pages read.

where.historical_name: Upper Amazon (pre-Columbian; no polity named in sources read)

importance.justification: Earliest known cacao use and an identified domestication centre.
